subject: Transportation Systems
title: Moscow's Palace Stations
description: A micro-lesson that makes Moscow's Palace Stations usable.

hook.text: Moscow's metro stations look like underground palaces—marble walls, chandeliers, bronze sculptures.

buildup.text: Stalin ordered them built as 'palaces for the people' to showcase Soviet grandeur.

discovery.text: Each station has a unique architectural theme. Komsomolskaya features baroque ceilings and gold mosaics.

twist.text: The beauty was also propaganda—proving communism could outshine capitalist cities.

climax.text: Today tourists visit Moscow's metro as a museum. The art survived despite the ideology that commissioned it.

punchline.text: Moscow built art galleries that happen to move trains.

quiz.question: Why were Moscow's metro stations built so lavishly?
options: As 'palaces for the people' showcasing Soviet power
